newsitem.title: EGYPT: UAE says Iran must give back "occupied" islands.
newsitem.headline: UAE says Iran must give back "occupied" islands.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates said on Monday that Iran had the right to take part in any Gulf security arrangements but only after giving back disputed islands.
"Iran is a Gulf state and has the right to participate in any arrangements in the Gulf," UAE Foreign Minister Rashid Abdullah al-Nuaimi told reporters.
"But before this, there should be good intentions and policies that serve regional stability and security," said Nuaimi after meeting Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
Since 1992 Iran and the UAE have been at loggerheads over Abu Musa and the Greater and Lesser Tunb islands that are close to key oil shipping lanes at the mouth of the Gulf.

"How do you cooperate in the security field with another party, while it occupies your land," Nuaimi said. "Iran is in this stage occupying Arab lands and refuses to go into negotiations to give these occupied Arab islands back."
Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati told a news conference in Riyadh on Sunday the dispute should be settled through negotiation.

"We have always voiced our readiness to enter direct negotiations with the United Arab Emirates...We have not closed the doors and we see that if there is a problem it should be solved within the framework of negotiations," he said.

Iran and UAE member Sharjah run Abu Musa jointly under an agreement reached in 1971 before the departure of British forces. In 1992, Iran tightened control over Abu Musa, citing security reasons. The UAE reacted by reviving its claim to the islands and accusing Iran of occupying them.
Iran says its sovereignty over the islands is not negotiable.
